title: Editing Tips — Audio + MIDI
intro: The tricks in this section work identically on audio regions and MIDI regions. Learn them once and you have doubled their value.

tips.t: Trim to the playhead from either direction
tips.d: The commands are “Set Region/Event/Marquee Start to Playhead Position” and the matching End command — search Key Commands (⌥K) for “Playhead Position” and put them on keys. (Note that on audio regions the Start command also moves the region anchor to the playhead.) Related one-shot trims live under Edit > Trim, such as Region End to Next Region. No mouse precision needed.

tips.t: Turn on “Snap Regions to Absolute Value”
tips.d: In the Snap menu. “Snap Regions to Absolute Value” is Logic's default: move or edit an item and it snaps exactly to the nearest grid position, ignoring any offset it had. The opposite is not an off switch but a second menu item, “Snap Regions to Relative Value” — choose that when you are moving a region that sits deliberately off‑grid, so it keeps its distance from the grid (a region at 2.1.1.16 moved one beat forward lands on 2.2.1.16, not 2.2.1.1).

tips.t: Esc opens the tool menu, Esc twice returns to the pointer
tips.d: T opens the Tool menu at the pointer — Apple's default assignment for Show Tool Menu — and pressing T twice puts you straight back on the Pointer tool. Fastest tool switching in the program. (Esc-based tool switching was the Logic 9 way and is no longer the default.)

Hold ⌘ to temporarily switch to the Command‑click tool; let go and you are instantly back on your Left‑click tool. Set it from the Command‑click Tool menu (the right‑hand one in the Tracks area menu bar) — most editors put Marquee there, and it is hard to beat.

tips.t: Assign the Fade tool to ⌘ when doing audio cleanup
tips.d: Set the secondary tool via the right‑hand tool menu, then every ⌘‑drag across a region edge creates a fade.

tips.t: Select everything after this point in one keystroke
tips.d: ⇧F is Select All Following: it grabs every region after the current selection, across all tracks — the fastest way to shift a whole song later. To stay on one track, use Edit > Select > All Following of Same Track, which already has a default key command of ⌥⇧F.

tips.t: Select equal or similar regions in one command
tips.d: Edit > Select > Similar Regions, Equal Regions (⇧E) and Equal Colored Regions (⇧C) find all matching regions across the project instantly — colour-code your parts and you can grab every one of them with a single keystroke. If you use Similar Regions often, check or set its key command in the Key Commands window (⌥K).

tips.t: Lock a region so you cannot move it by accident
tips.d: Control-click a region and choose Lock SMPTE Position to pin it to its absolute time position, so later tempo changes cannot drag it out of sync — note this locks it against tempo, not against your mouse. To stop edits altogether, use the track's Protect button: click the padlock and it turns green, and any attempt to change that track raises a “track is locked” dialog. It is not shown by default (track headers start with Mute, Solo and Record Enable), so switch it on by Control-clicking the track header and choosing Track Header Components, or via Track > Configure Track Header.
